proposal: The Mandate recommends that the Forest Service shift from reliance on fire toward proactive vegetation management (thinning, removing live fuels and deadwood) and increase timber sales. It calls for embracing and building on Executive Order 13855 and working with Congress to cut NEPA and Endangered Species Act obstacles to fuel reduction.

status_summary: Executive Order 14225 (2025-03-01) directed expanded timber production and streamlined consultation and NEPA review, and Executive Order 14308 (2025-06-12) directed consolidation of federal wildland fire programs and reviews of rules that impede prevention. USDA announced a $200 million national active forest management strategy on 2025-05-29 with a goal of 25 percent more national forest harvest and 4 billion board feet annually by fiscal year 2028. In 2026 the Forest Service proposed rescinding the 2001 Roadless Rule (2026-08-20), Interior finalized two BLM timber categorical exclusions (2026-08-20), and on 2026-10-13 the Forest Service published a final rule shortening and simplifying its project objection process, effective 2026-11-12. No verified data on timber sold or harvested since 2025 were found, so results are not yet shown.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14225, Immediate Expansion of American Timber Production, is signed; it sets 30 to 280 day deadlines for timber guidance, ESA consultation strategy, annual sale targets and NEPA categorical exclusions (published 2025-03-06).

USDA announces $23 million in grants to move hazardous fuels to processing facilities, giving priority to areas under Emergency Situation Determinations, and references the Secretary's directive to increase active forest management.

Secretary Rollins announces $200 million to implement the National Active Forest Management Strategy, with goals of 25 percent more national forest timber harvest and 4 billion board feet annually by fiscal year 2028.

Executive Order 14308, Empowering Commonsense Wildfire Prevention and Response, is signed; it directs consolidation of Interior and Agriculture wildland fire programs and review of rules that hinder prevention (published 2025-06-18).

USDA opens public comment on rescinding the 2001 Roadless Rule and announces an environmental impact statement; the rescission would cover about 45 million of nearly 60 million inventoried roadless acres.
The Forest Service publishes a proposed rule to streamline its project-level predecisional administrative review (objection) process.
The Forest Service consolidates national fire and aviation authorities under a single Deputy Chief for Fire and Aviation Management.

USDA publishes a proposed rule to rescind the 2001 Roadless Rule (comments due in September or October 2026, with conflicting dates listed); Interior announces two finalized NEPA categorical exclusions for BLM timber salvage and thinning projects up to 5,000 acres.

The Forest Service publishes a final rule revising its project-level predecisional objection process (91 FR 64760, 36 CFR part 218), shortening comment, objection and response periods, moving public notice to USDA websites and electronic notification, and aligning the process with USDA NEPA procedures; effective 2026-11-12.

title: Expand active forest management, timber sales and wildfire fuel reduction
uncertainties: The Forest Service's emergency situation determinations were referenced in a USDA release but the acreage and any litigation were not verified. Timber sale and harvest volumes since 2025 were not found, and the Fix Our Forests Act or other forest legislation was not checked (the legislation page returned an error). The Mandate recommendation to embrace Executive Order 13855 was not matched to an explicit reinstatement; the match is based on the content of Executive Orders 14225 and 14308. Roadless rule comment deadlines appear with two different dates in the sources, and the rescission is a proposal, not final. Interior's categorical exclusions apply to BLM land, which falls under chapter 16 rather than Forest Service land.
